knowledge: Cornelia de Lange syndrome 6 (CdLS6, OMIM #620568) is an ultra-rare autosomal dominant form of CdLS caused by heterozygous de novo variants in the bromodomain-containing protein 4 gene (BRD4). The landmark paper identifying BRD4 variants in CdLS was published by Olley et al. in 2018 (PMID: 30054598, Nature Genetics). Unlike classical CdLS caused by NIPBL mutations, which frequently presents with severe reduction defects of the upper limbs, distinctive arched eyebrows with synophrys, thick eyelashes, microcephaly, and profound intrauterine growth restriction, BRD4-related CdLS is generally reported as a milder or atypical CdLS phenotype. Documented cases often feature intellectual disability/developmental delay, mild facial gestalt reminiscent of CdLS (such as synophrys, long philtrum, thin upper lip), microcephaly, and growth restriction, but typically lack severe limb reduction defects (e.g., absent forearms or oligodactyly).
prior_hypothesis: Clinically distinguishing CdLS6 (BRD4) from classical CdLS (NIPBL) and other cohesinopathy-related subtypes purely on phenotype relies on a non-classical presentation: patients manifest mild-to-moderate developmental delay/intellectual disability and subtle CdLS facial features (synophrys, arched eyebrows, low posterior hairline, depressed nasal bridge) combined with microcephaly and small stature, but almost uniformly lack the severe limb reduction anomalies (such as acheiria, adactyly, or phocomelia) characteristic of classical NIPBL-related CdLS. Differentiation from other non-classical cohesinopathies (e.g., SMC1A, SMC3, RAD21, HDAC8) cannot be reliably achieved by dysmorphology alone and requires molecular genetic confirmation.

candidate_answers.answer: In the foundational cohort reported by Olley et al. 2018 (PMID: 30054598), 4 individuals with de novo BRD4 variants were described. Phenotypic frequencies included intellectual disability/developmental delay (HP:0001249) in 4/4 (100%), microcephaly (HP:0000252) in 4/4 (100%), synophrys (HP:0000664) or arched eyebrows in 4/4 (100%), short stature/postnatal growth retardation (HP:0004322) in 3/4 (75%), and minor digital/extremity anomalies (such as clinodactyly HP:0030084 or small hands/feet HP:0200055) in 3/4 (75%).

The most discriminating phenotypic features between CdLS6 (BRD4) and classical CdLS (NIPBL) are the absence of severe upper-limb reduction defects (e.g., phocomelia, oligodactyly, absent ulna/radius) and less severe visceral/diaphragmatic defects, presenting instead with subtle CdLS facies and mild-to-moderate neurodevelopmental impairment. Compared to non-specific syndromic intellectual disabilities (such as Coffin-Siris syndrome or Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome), the combination of synophrys, long smooth philtrum with thin vermilion of the upper lip, and microcephaly provides the strongest clue, though clinical distinction from RAD21- or SMC3-related CdLS is of low confidence without sequencing.

Severe congenital structural limb amputations/transverse reduction defects (e.g., acheiria, missing digits, severe radial ray defects) are considered absent in confirmed BRD4-CdLS cases; their presence strongly argues in favor of NIPBL-associated classical CdLS rather than CdLS6.

Genotype-phenotype correlations for BRD4 remain poorly established due to the extremely small number of reported cases (fewer than 10-15 published individuals globally). Reported variants include missense and truncating/frameshift variants affecting bromodomains or the extraterminal (ET) domain, with no definitive sex-specific or age-specific phenotypic divergence clearly characterized beyond standard developmental progression.

assumptions: Assuming the query specifically concerns germline/de novo heterozygous variants in BRD4 causing Cornelia de Lange syndrome 6 (OMIM #620568), excluding somatic BRD4 alterations implicated in NUT midline carcinoma or hematologic malignancies.
Assuming that clinical criteria defined by the international CdLS consensus group (Kline et al. 2018, Nature Reviews Genetics) apply for scoring classical vs non-classical CdLS features.
Assuming published cohorts describing BRD4 germline phenotypes are limited to a small number of series and case reports, primarily anchored by Olley et al. 2018.
